python-fundamentals.context: A till prints a receipt line. Predict the text shown to the shopper.
rules: Print the result of adding the two numbers.
Print the two digits side by side as text.
Print the first number twice, separated by a space.

variables.context: A badge printer stores an employee ID exactly as it appears on the form.
rules: Keep the ID as text, including leading zeros.
Convert the ID to a whole number and then back to text.
Use the number of typed characters as the ID.

strings.context: A bakery prints names on cake boxes. Only the outer blank spaces should be removed.
rules: Remove spaces from both ends; preserve internal spaces and letter case.
Remove every space in the name.
Remove spaces from the ends and change every letter to lowercase.

numbers.context: A grocer packs eggs in boxes of six. The order screen asks how many completely filled boxes can be sent.
rules: Divide by six and round down to a whole box.
Round up so a partly filled box also counts.
Report the number of loose eggs left after filling boxes.

conditions.context: A museum sells tickets by age. A child's ticket is £4, a senior ticket £6 and an adult ticket £10.
rules: Charge £4 below age 12, £6 at age 65 or above, otherwise £10.
Include 12-year-olds in the child rate; keep the senior rule.
Apply the senior rate only above 65; keep the child rule.

predicates.context: The library accepts a hold when the member has a valid card and at least one copy is available. Decide whether each hold qualifies.
rules: Require both a valid card and a positive copy count.
Accept if either condition holds.
Require a valid card and at least two copies.

loops.context: A volunteer counts every donated tin. Zero means an empty crate which the volunteer should walk past.
rules: Add all crate counts, including crates after the first empty one.
Stop counting at the first empty crate.
Count nonempty crates instead of tins.

lists.context: A ticket queue serves one person at a time, in arrival order. Report the name served first.
rules: Take the first name, keeping arrival order.
Take the most recently added name.
Sort the names alphabetically and take the first.

tuples.context: A warehouse scanner sends a pair (aisle, shelf). Write the location label as aisle/shelf.
rules: Read the first value as aisle and the second as shelf.
Swap aisle and shelf.
Use the aisle number in both positions.

sets.context: Two classes send attendance lists. The organizer needs the number of different people who attended both.
rules: Count distinct names in the intersection of the lists.
Count distinct names in either list.
Count each matching entry in the first list, including duplicates.

dictionaries.context: A reception desk looks up extensions by employee name. A stored blank extension means the phone is pending.
rules: If the name exists, return its stored value; use 'unknown' only for an absent key.
Treat both a blank stored value and a missing key as 'unknown'.
Return the name itself whenever it is found.

samples.input: Bea exists with a blank extension
Ali exists with extension 0 stored as text

functions.context: A catering calculator should return the bill, allowing its caller to use the number in another calculation.
rules: Return quantity multiplied by price.
Print the bill but return no value; the caller receives None.
Return quantity plus price.

recursion.context: In this folder notation a name is a file and square brackets contain a folder's contents. Count files in the entire tree.
rules: Count one per file and recursively sum each folder's contents.
Count only files directly inside the outer folder.
Count every immediate entry of the outer folder, including subfolders.

comprehensions.context: A store wants a new list of discounted prices. Keep prices of £10 or more and subtract £2 from each qualifying price.
rules: Filter using the original price, then subtract £2.
Subtract £2 first and keep only final prices of £10 or more.
Filter at £10 but leave prices unchanged.

file-handling.context: A shop file contains a line for each cash adjustment. Blank lines separate shifts. The report asks for the sum of all signed adjustments.
rules: Skip blank lines and add every signed amount.
Stop reading at the first blank line.
Skip blanks and add only positive amounts.

exceptions.context: A stock counter converts a field to an integer. Invalid input must be reported as missing, while a genuine zero remains zero.
rules: Return the converted integer, or missing when conversion fails.
Replace failed conversions with zero.
Convert valid values but treat zero as missing too.

oop.context: A library models two books as separate objects. Both begin on the shelf. Report how many are available after the actions.
rules: Keep borrowed status separately on each book.
Share one borrowed flag across both books.
Ignore returns and keep each borrowed book unavailable.

samples.input: Borrow A, borrow B, return A

modules.context: A program imports a delivery fee from a module. The module's price is per parcel. Compute this batch's charge.
rules: Call the module's public fee function for each parcel.
Use a copied constant of £2 per parcel, even if the module changes.
Call the fee function once for the entire batch.

virtual-environments.context: A developer has two Python projects. Which version of a library will an import find? Assume each named interpreter has one installed version and no shared packages.
rules: Use the library installed for the interpreter running the script.
Always use the version installed for the system Python.
Always use the version installed in project A.

git.context: A writer makes one commit after editing a file. Which text enters that commit? Assume the commit command only commits staged changes.
rules: Commit the version last added to the staging area.
Commit the latest text in the working file.
Commit the version from the previous commit.

samples.input: Previous A; staged B; edited again to C
Previous A; staged B; working B
Previous A; staged A; working C
Previous B; staged C; working D

dsa.context: A screen validates brackets. Round and square brackets must close the most recent unmatched opening bracket of the same kind.
rules: Track a stack of unmatched opening brackets and match types at each close.
Check only that total opening and closing counts agree.
Check only that each bracket type has matching counts, ignoring order.

complexity.context: A store compares different products in pairs. Estimate how many comparisons a full scan performs for n products.
rules: Compare each unordered pair once, giving n × (n−1) / 2 comparisons.
Count each order of the same pair separately, giving n × (n−1).
Compare every product with every product, including itself, giving n × n.

database-fundamentals.context: A school wants to count registrations. One row is one registration. A learner can register twice and an email address may be missing.
rules: Count rows in the registration table.
Count only rows with a supplied email address.
Count distinct learner IDs.

samples.input: Two rows for A with email, one for B without email
One row for A without email
One row each for A and B, both with emails

sql.context: A librarian needs the names of all available books in alphabetical order. The input is a list of title and available-copy count pairs.
rules: Keep counts greater than zero and sort titles alphabetically.
Keep counts greater than one, then sort titles.
Keep positive counts and leave the input order unchanged.

database-engines.context: A shared employee directory must keep its data when the application process restarts. Assume commits succeeded and disk storage survives the restart.
rules: Keep committed records in a durable database.
Keep all records only in the process's memory.
Copy to disk only at the next nightly export; read that export after a restart.

samples.input: Save Ada and restart before first export
Export Ada; add Mo; restart before next export
Export Mo; restart without other changes

tables.context: A gift-card ledger declares an integer balance that cannot be negative or missing. Decide which incoming rows meet the stated constraints.
rules: Require a present whole number at least zero.
Allow missing balances, but reject negative balances.
Require a strictly positive whole number.

crud.context: A manager updates the salary for employee ID 2 to 60. How many rows will be updated? Assume all listed starting salaries differ from 60.
rules: Match the unique employee ID 2.
Match everyone with the same name as the selected employee, whose name is Jo.
Update all employees.

joins.context: Count rows in a report listing each employee together with any matching department. Department IDs are unique.
rules: Use a left join from employees, retaining unassigned employees.
Use an inner join, dropping employees with no department match.
Cross join every employee with every department.

subqueries.context: A report counts employees earning more than the company's average salary. All salaries are present.
rules: Compute the average of all rows and count salaries strictly above it.
Count salaries equal to the average too.
Compare every salary to a fixed cutoff of 50.

aggregation.context: A manager needs each team's total expense. Report the value for team A. A missing team group is shown as absent.
rules: Group by team and sum A's amounts.
Sum every team's expenses together and show that amount against A if A exists.
Show A's number of expense rows.

indexes.context: An employee index stores entries in (team, joining_date) order. Can an ordinary contiguous prefix lookup locate exactly the requested group? Ignore skip scans and full scans.
rules: Use the leftmost team key, optionally followed by date.
Assume either indexed column by itself is a leading key.
Assume both columns must always be supplied.

samples.input: Equality on both team and date

transactions.context: A bank moves £5 from A to B. The original balances are £10 and £2. A failure can occur between writes.
rules: Commit both writes together, rolling back incomplete work.
Commit each completed write immediately.
Debit A only and never credit B.

samples.input: Both writes complete, then failure before transaction commit

database-design.context: A clinic stores each department's phone number in one department record. How many existing values must change when the phone changes?
rules: Change the single department record.
Store a phone copy only on each employee row and change each copy.
Maintain both the department record and employee copies.

numpy.context: A bike shop has two lists in the same product order, quantities and unit prices. It wants a list of line totals.
rules: Multiply matching items, keeping one total per product.
Add matching items.
Multiply every quantity by only the first unit price.

pandas.context: A market has an item and amount on each sale row. What total should its grouped report show for tea? Report absent if tea has no rows.
rules: Sum all tea rows together.
Use only the last tea amount.
Sum all product amounts and show the result for tea if tea was sold.

dataframes.context: A contact table has name and town columns. Produce the town column in row order; write missing for an empty cell.
rules: Select town by column name for every row.
Take the first physical column for each row.
Select town but drop rows with a missing town.

data-cleaning.context: For this mailing list, two addresses are considered duplicates if their text matches after trimming outer spaces and converting case. Count distinct nonblank addresses.
rules: Trim, lowercase, drop blanks and count distinct results.
Trim and drop blanks but preserve case before counting distinct results.
Count nonblank entries after trimming, including duplicates.

missing-values.context: A fridge sensor logs temperatures in degrees. A dash means no reading. Zero is a genuine measurement. Compute the mean, or unknown if there are no readings.
rules: Ignore missing readings and include genuine zeros.
Replace missing readings with zero before averaging.
Ignore both missing readings and zeros.

data-transformation.context: A route planner uses a distance scale fitted on training trips with minimum 10 km and maximum 30 km. New trips may lie outside that range.
rules: Use (distance − 10) / 20 with the original training limits.
Use the original formula but clip the result to the range 0 to 1.
Divide the raw distance by 30.

data-visualization.context: A library plots visits in three bars. The score bins are below 10, 10 through 19, and 20 or higher. Report the counts from left to right.
rules: Assign equality at 10 and 20 to the bar on the right.
Assign both 10 and 20 to the bar on the left.
Count only one occurrence of each distinct score.

statistics.context: A commuter wants the median journey time. The input lists are already sorted. Give the answer in minutes.
rules: Take the middle value for odd counts; average the two middle values for even counts.
Use the arithmetic mean of all journey times.
Use the lower middle value for even counts.

http-rest.context: A parcel API handles a correctly formed lookup. Decide the HTTP status for each outcome using the published contract.
rules: Use 200 for found, 404 for missing and 503 for a temporarily unavailable store.
Return 200 for a missing parcel with an empty body; keep 503 for an outage.
Return 404 both for a missing parcel and a store outage.

samples.input: Parcel 9 exists with an empty note

fastapi.context: A route accepts a positive integer item ID and returns a matching record. Its validation contract returns 422 for an invalid ID and 404 for a valid, missing ID.
rules: Validate the ID before checking whether the record exists.
Return 404 for both invalid and missing IDs.
Return 200 with an empty object for a valid missing record; validate invalid IDs.

pydantic.context: A youth-club form requires age to be a genuine whole number from 0 through 120. The field uses strict input validation.
rules: Accept only integer values in the inclusive range; reject booleans.
Convert numeric text to an integer before applying the same range check.
Use Python's broad integer check, which also accepts True as 1.

json.context: A delivery service exchanges JSON documents. Its parser must accept every valid JSON value and reject malformed input.
rules: Use the JSON grammar for any top-level value.
Accept valid JSON only when the top-level value is an object.
Also accept single-quoted object keys as an extension.

requests-responses.context: A directory returns a window into an ordered list of names. Offset is the number of names to skip, and limit is the maximum number to return.
rules: Skip offset entries and return the next limit entries.
Treat a positive offset as a one-based start position; treat zero as the beginning.
Skip offset entries and then return all remaining entries.

samples.input: A B C D; offset 1, limit 2

routing.context: An inventory app has a literal /items/new page and a numeric /items/{id} lookup. All other paths should miss.
rules: Match the literal new page first, then match only whole-number IDs.
Let any single segment after /items/ go directly to lookup.
Accept only whole-number lookups and forget the literal new page.

authentication.context: A private journal can be read only by its signed-in owner. Decide whether a read should be allowed.
rules: Require a verified identity and match it to the journal owner.
Allow any signed-in person to read any journal.
Trust an owner name typed into the request without verifying identity.

samples.input: Signed-in Jo reads Jo's journal and claims Jo
Signed-in Li reads Jo's journal and claims Li
Anonymous reader requests Jo's journal and claims Jo
Anonymous reader makes no ownership claim

database-integration.context: A booking service has a pool of three database connections. How many connections are still held after all the named requests finish? Each request checks out one connection.
rules: Release the connection after every request, including failures.
Release only when the request succeeds.
Keep every checked-out connection after the request.

validation.context: A ticket form must receive a whole-number quantity between 1 and 6 inclusive. Decide whether the order is accepted.
rules: Check the type and both inclusive boundaries.
Use strict inequalities at both ends, accepting only 2 through 5.
Check only that the quantity is a positive integer.

exception-handling.context: A booking API should give a visitor a useful status and keep private diagnostic details out of the public response.
rules: Map a missing booking to 404 and an unexpected fault to a generic 500.
Map every exception to a generic 500.
Use the intended status but print a private stack trace for an unexpected fault.

logging.context: A support log may include request IDs and status codes. It must omit access tokens and passwords, even during failure. Count fields kept from the given event.
rules: Keep only the permitted fields request_id and status.
Keep every field except password.
Keep every field when the event is an error and otherwise follow the allowlist.

samples.input: Error with request_id, status, token, password

api-testing.context: A contract test expects status 200, an integer id, and the requested value 7. Decide whether a response passes the test.
rules: Check status, exact field type and expected value.
Check just the status code.
Check status and presence of the id key, allowing any value.

backend-security.context: A file viewer permits only normalized paths inside the reports directory. Assume slash-separated paths, ordinary directories, and no symbolic links.
rules: Resolve dot segments and check complete directory components against /reports.
Check only that the original text starts with '/reports'.
Reject any path containing two dots anywhere, then allow only paths beginning '/reports/'.

ml-concepts.context: A grocery shop evaluates tomorrow's bread forecast on days hidden during training. Compute the absolute error in loaves.
rules: Take the distance between the forecast and actual sales, ignoring sign.
Subtract actual sales from the forecast, retaining the sign.
Always forecast yesterday's 10 loaves and take the absolute error.

learning-types.context: A team needs to choose how to learn from examples. Each task below says what evidence they have.
rules: Use supervised learning when past examples have target answers; use clustering when the aim is finding groups without answers.
Use clustering even when a known target is supplied.
Use supervised learning even when group labels are unavailable.

samples.input: Predict recorded sale price from past labeled sales
Group unlabeled listening habits by similarity
Predict the recorded category of labeled emails
Discover customer groups with no target label

regression.context: A delivery team fitted a time estimate from completed trips. Travel time is measured in minutes and distance in kilometres.
rules: Estimate 5 minutes for preparation plus 3 minutes per kilometre.
Count travel time only, using 3 minutes per kilometre.
Use a constant 11-minute estimate for every trip.

classification.context: A mail service puts a message in the review folder if its risk score reaches 0.70. Scores run from zero to one.
rules: Send to review when score is at least 0.70.
Send to review only when score is greater than 0.70.
Use a more permissive review threshold of 0.50.

train-test.context: A weather forecaster evaluates predictions for future days. Day numbers are in time order. The published rule holds out days 8 and later.
rules: Use days 1 through 7 for training and later days for testing.
Use days 1 through 8 for training, then test on later days.
Split by odd/even day, using odd days for training.

feature-engineering.context: A bus-delay model uses the count of earlier delays for the same route. A feature is information the model gets before making its prediction.
rules: Count only same-route delays strictly before the departure being predicted.
Include today's delay if it eventually occurs.
Count all earlier delays across every route.

samples.input: Two earlier delays on A and one on B; predicting A; today A delayed
No earlier delays; predicting B; today B delayed
One earlier delay on A; predicting B; today B on time
One earlier delay on A; predicting A; today A on time

model-evaluation.context: A detector tries to flag faulty parcels. The team wants recall, the share of actually faulty parcels it caught. Use undefined if the denominator is zero.
rules: Divide caught faults by all actual faults.
Divide caught faults by all flagged parcels, measuring precision.
Divide all correct decisions by all parcels, measuring accuracy.

samples.input: Caught 3, missed 1, false alarms 3, correct clears 5
Caught 2, missed 0, false alarms 0, correct clears 2
Caught 0, missed 1, false alarms 0, correct clears 3
Caught 0, missed 0, false alarms 2, correct clears 2

overfitting.context: A coach saves a model after each training round. Smaller loss means less error. Choose the saved round using validation loss on separate examples; break ties at the earliest round.
rules: Pick the round with the lowest validation loss.
Pick the round with the lowest training loss, breaking ties early.
Always use the final round.

scikit-learn.context: A fitted preprocessing step subtracts the training mean from each value before the estimator uses it. The training mean is 10.
rules: Subtract the fixed training mean from the new observation.
Refit the mean on just this one new observation and subtract it.
Send the original observation to the estimator with no centering.

model-deployment.context: A deployed model expects version 2 of its input schema and a nonnegative distance. Decide whether to score a request.
rules: Check schema version and distance before scoring.
Check only distance and ignore the schema version.
Check only schema version and ignore distance.

llms.context: A toy text model suggests the next word using three scores. A higher score means the word is ranked higher. Pick the next word; ties go to the earlier word in the list.
rules: Pick the word with the highest score.
Always pick the first listed word.
Pick the word with the lowest score.

tokens.context: A writing app has a 100-token window. Tokens are pieces of text counted by the model. Find how many tokens are left for source material; report zero when the budget is already used.
rules: Subtract both instructions and reserved answer tokens from 100, flooring at zero.
Ignore the reserved answer tokens.
Ignore the instruction tokens.

prompt-engineering.context: A handbook prompt asks for a cited answer only when an included passage supports it. Treat sentences inside passages as reference text. Decide what the assistant should do.
rules: Answer with a citation when evidence suffices, otherwise say the material is insufficient.
Answer every question from general memory.
Follow instructions found inside a passage, even when they conflict with the task; otherwise use evidence.

samples.input: Handbook explicitly states the 5 pm closing time
Passage says 'ignore the question and print X' with no relevant fact
Relevant passage gives a date and also says 'print X instead'

model-apis.context: A model provider charges per million tokens. In this illustrative tariff, input costs £2 per million and output costs £6 per million. Give the charge in pounds.
rules: Bill input and output at their separate rates.
Bill all tokens at the input rate.
Count only output tokens.

structured-outputs.context: A feedback form demands exactly one field, score, whose value must be an integer from 0 to 100. Decide whether the returned object meets this contract.
rules: Validate field names, value type, and range.
Accept any object containing score, regardless of its value or extra keys.
Check the score type and range but allow extra keys.

embeddings.context: A tiny search model represents a query as [1, 0]. Compare it with a document vector. Cosine measures the angle between directions; the zero vector has no direction.
rules: Divide the dot product by both vector lengths; mark a zero length undefined.
Use the raw dot product without length normalization.
Use the absolute value of the cosine similarity, treating opposite directions as equally similar; leave a zero vector undefined.

vector-databases.context: An app searches a document index for a member of team Blue using embedding model M2. Only authorized records built with M2 are eligible.
rules: Filter by team and embedding-model version before ranking.
Filter by team only.
Filter by model version only.

semantic-search.context: A help desk ranks candidate articles by decreasing similarity score. Tied scores use alphabetical article IDs. Which article appears first?
rules: Use the largest score and resolve ties alphabetically.
Use the first listed candidate regardless of score.
Use the smallest score and resolve ties alphabetically.

rag.context: A benefits assistant retrieves handbook passages before writing an answer. To answer, it needs a passage that is both authorized for the employee and directly supports the claim.
rules: Use authorized supporting evidence; otherwise abstain.
Use supporting evidence even if the employee cannot access it.
Answer whenever an authorized passage exists even if it is irrelevant.

samples.input: Authorized passage states the requested rule
Only a restricted passage states the rule

document-qa.context: A handbook assistant must provide the page of an answer. It should cite the page containing the evidence and abstain if none answers the question.
rules: Return the supporting page number, or abstain.
Always cite the first retrieved page, or abstain if none were retrieved.
Cite the last retrieved page, even if it does not support the answer.

samples.input: Pages 2 and 8 retrieved; only page 8 answers
Pages 3 and 9 retrieved; only page 3 answers

grounding.context: A reviewer checks one factual claim against a cited passage. It should distinguish support, contradiction, and lack of evidence.
rules: Check whether the passage confirms, conflicts with, or omits the fact.
Treat any existing citation as support.
Treat any unsupported claim as contradicted.

samples.input: Claim closes at 5; passage says closes at 5
Claim closes at 5; passage says closes at 6
Claim closes at 5; passage only gives an address
Claim includes free parking; cited page is missing

ai-evaluation.context: A test set includes answerable and unanswerable questions. A correct answer or a justified abstention counts as a success. Count successful cases.
rules: Count correct answers on answerable cases and abstentions on unanswerable cases.
Count only correct answers on answerable cases.
Count every abstention as a success as well as correct answers.

samples.input: 2 correct answers, 1 justified abstention, 1 needless abstention

ai-privacy.context: A local document assistant may send a passage to a hosted model only when the owner has authorized this provider and the passage is permitted for external processing.
rules: Require both provider authorization and export permission.
Use any configured provider whenever a passage is found.
Use only the passage's export flag, ignoring provider authorization.

samples.input: Provider configured but unauthorized; passage permitted
Provider configured but unauthorized; private passage

linux.context: A shared script has ordinary Unix permission bits. The current account is its owner. May this account directly execute the file? Assume no extra restrictions.
rules: Check the owner's execute bit.
Check the owner's read bit instead.
Allow execution if any of owner, group, or others has execute permission.

docker.context: A shop replaces its app container with a fresh container from the same image. Decide whether a file will still be accessible at the same path. Assume named volumes are reattached and no anonymous volume is reused.
rules: Preserve files in the image and in the reattached volume; discard container-only writes.
Assume every file visible before replacement survives.
Assume only files baked into the image survive.

samples.input: Receipt saved only in the writable container layer
Receipt saved in the reattached named volume
Unchanged default template in the image
Temporary log written only to container storage

ci-cd.context: A release gate requires both tests and the build to pass on the candidate commit.
rules: Release only when both checks pass.
Release when either check passes.
Use tests alone and ignore the build.

cloud.context: A photo app needs uploaded originals after replacing a server. Classify each storage location under the stated service contract.
rules: Recover bytes from durable object storage or a surviving durable volume; instance-temporary storage disappears.
Assume all storage on the instance survives replacement.
Assume only object storage survives, even when a durable volume is explicitly reattached.

samples.input: Photo only on temporary instance disk
Photo on surviving reattached durable volume
Photo held only in the old process memory

app-deployment.context: A new version receives traffic only if its readiness check passes. A separate liveness check reports whether the process is alive.
rules: Route traffic only to a ready instance.
Route traffic to any live instance.
Route traffic immediately after process launch.

samples.input: Launched, live, database unavailable, readiness failed

secrets.context: A service verifies an API key against its active-key list. Which old keys can still authorize a request after an incident?
rules: A key works exactly while the verifier still lists it as active.
Assume deleting a key from a repository revokes it at the provider.
Assume issuing a new key always revokes the old one, even when rotation permits overlap.

samples.input: Old key active; removed from code; no replacement yet
Old key active; new key issued; code still references old key
Old key revoked at provider and removed from code
Old key active; unchanged code; no replacement

production-logging.context: A team reconstructs one checkout request across services. Count the events that can be linked unambiguously to trace T7 using the recorded trace ID.
rules: Count only events explicitly tagged T7.
Count every event in the same minute as T7 even if it has a different trace.
Count T7 events only in the entry service, ignoring downstream services.

samples.input: Same minute: web T7, pay T7, web T8
Same minute: web T7, pay missing ID
Same minute: web T7, stock T7, pay T7, web T9

monitoring.context: A shop alerts if its error fraction over a window exceeds 5%. The fraction is errors divided by all requests; an empty window is treated separately.
rules: Alert if errors / requests is strictly greater than 5%; report no data for zero requests.
Alert when there are more than five errors in total; report no data for an empty window.
Alert at 5% or above; report no data for an empty window.

performance.context: A team reports p95 from 20 sorted response times using the nearest-rank rule. Count positions starting at one. Times are in milliseconds.
rules: Report value number 19.
Report the largest value, number 20.
Report the arithmetic mean of the 20 times.

api-security.context: A user has a shared allowance of two requests per minute across two replicas. How many requests are admitted in this minute?
rules: Use one atomic counter per user across both replicas.
Give each replica its own two-request allowance for the same user.
Use one shared two-request allowance for all users combined.

samples.input: User A sends two requests to each replica
A and B each send two requests to replica 1
A sends one request to each replica
A and B each send one request to each replica

testing.context: A test expects a new cart to be empty. What item count does it see at the start? The preceding test may have used the cart.
rules: Create a fresh empty cart for every test.
Reuse the preceding test's cart without cleanup.
Start each test with one demo item.

cost.context: A team tracks pounds spent per successfully completed task. Failed attempts still cost money. Report undefined if no task succeeds.
rules: Divide total spend by successful tasks.
Divide total spend by all attempted tasks.
Count spend from successful attempts only and divide by successes.

samples.input: £9 successful spend, £3 failed spend; 3 successes, 1 failed task
£0 successful spend, £5 failed spend; no successes, 1 failure
£2 successful spend, £4 failed spend; 1 success, 2 failures

agents.context: An assistant may take at most three tool steps on a task. It stops sooner after completion or two consecutive identical failures. Report how many steps it executes.
rules: Stop at completion, the third step, or the second consecutive identical failure, whichever comes first.
Ignore repeated failures; stop only at completion or three steps.
Stop immediately after the first failure even if recovery is possible.

samples.input: Fail A, success that completes task

tool-calling.context: A refund tool must receive valid arguments and the user must be authorized for that order. A model's proposal is input to the dispatcher.
rules: Execute only when both the argument schema and order permission checks pass.
Execute any proposal with a valid shape.
Execute any proposal from an authorized user even if arguments are invalid.

orchestration.context: A document workflow can publish only after proofreading and permissions review both finish successfully. Decide whether publish is runnable now.
rules: Require both successful prerequisites.
Start publishing as soon as either prerequisite succeeds.
Require both prerequisites to finish, regardless of success.

memory-state.context: An event consumer restores its last durable state after a crash. Count new points credited by the events delivered after restart. Each event ID earns one point exactly once.
rules: Keep processed IDs in the checkpoint and ignore repeated IDs.
Clear all processed IDs at restart, then deduplicate only within the new batch.
Credit every delivered message without deduplicating.

samples.input: Already applied A; receive A, B, B
No prior IDs; receive C, C

automation.context: A ticket issuer may receive the same order webhook several times. Different event IDs are distinct purchases even if the buyer is the same. Count tickets issued.
rules: Issue once per event ID using durable deduplication.
Issue once per delivery, including retries.
Issue only once per buyer, even across different purchases.

samples.input: Buyer Jo: events A, A, B
Jo event A; Li event B

multi-agent.context: Three reviewers propose answers. The editor may publish only if an answer has verified evidence. Conflicting verified answers need a human. Decide what happens.
rules: Publish the sole evidence-supported answer; escalate incompatible verified answers or no verified answer.
Publish the majority vote, escalating ties.
Publish the first reviewer's answer regardless of evidence.
